correctness.rationale: For a connected dominating initial set of size at least two, at least one initially black vertex lies both in and outside any witnessing part. At the first force from part \(i\), the outside white count is at most \(k\); after that force, the remaining inside white count must also be at most \(k\). Initial black vertices on both sides sharpen the capacities to \(n_i-1\) and \(N-n_i-1\), yielding the lower bound, and choosing whites attaining both capacities gives the two-step construction. The singleton universal-vertex exception is exact. The inspected verifier brute-forces every multipartite type through order nine and every admissible \(k\), matching the formula.

originality.rationale: A previously published SCOPE record already classifies every standard \(k\)-forcing set of a complete multipartite graph by the identical first-force argument. Imposing connected domination on that all-set classification is elementary: size at least two means the black set meets at least two parts, which changes only the outside capacity from \(N-n_i\) to \(N-n_i-1\), plus the obvious universal-singleton exception. Thus the assigned minimum formula is implication-level covered by the prior all-k-forcing theorem and basic complete-multipartite connectivity/domination.
residual_risks: The rejection does not depend on whether an older external paper contains the same formula; the published SCOPE all-set theorem already covers it.
